Let $p\in X$ be a closed point other than the origin, and suppose that its stabilizer in the grading group $\Gm$ is exactly $\mu_M$. Let $Y$ be the closure of its $\Gm$-orbit, with reduced structure. Then $\C[Y]$ is concentrated in degrees divisible by $M$, the set $\{k:\C[Y]_{Mk}\ne0\}$ is a numerical semigroup (cofinite in $\Z_{\ge0}$), each nonzero $\C[Y]_{Mk}$ is a line, and $e_Y=1$ with $\delta=1$.

Let $GL_n$ act linearly on a vector space $U$, let $R=\C[U]^{SL_n}$ be graded so that $R_0=\C$, and let $\gamma$ be an odd integer such that every $B\in GL_n$ acts on $X=\Spec R$ as the grading element $(\det B)^\gamma$. Let $p\in X$ be a closed point other than the origin, fixed by a grading element $\eta$ of order $2^a$, and let $y\in U$ lie in the closed $SL_n$-orbit over $p$. Then there is a diagonalizable $A\in GL_n$ of finite two-power order with $A\cdot y=y$ and $\ord(\det A)=2^a$.

Let $p$ be a prime and $d=p^re$ with $p\nmid e$. In $\F_p[t]$, $\overline{\Phi_d}=\overline{\Phi_e}$ if $r=0$ and $\overline{\Phi_d}=\overline{\Phi_e}^{\,p^{r-1}(p-1)}$ if $r\ge1$. The roots of $\overline{\Phi_e}$ in $\overline\F_p$ are the elements of multiplicative order $e$, each simple.

Let $F,G\in\Q(t)\cap\Z[[t]]$ have all their poles at roots of unity, let $p$ be a prime, $p\nmid M$, and suppose $F\equiv G\pmod{p\Z[[t]]}$. Suppose $G$ has a pole of order $\delta\ge1$ at a primitive $M$-th root of unity $\zeta$, no pole at any primitive $Mp^r$-th root of unity for $r\ge1$, and that $C=\lim_{t\to\zeta}(1-t^M)^\delta G(t)$ is a unit in $\Z[\zeta]_{\mathfrak p}$ for some prime $\mathfrak p$ over $p$. Then $F$ has a pole at a primitive $Mp^r$-th root of unity for some $r\ge0$, hence at all of them; and every expression $F(t)=P(t)/\prod_i(1-t^{a_i})^{b_i}$ with $P\in\Q[t]$ and $a_i,b_i>0$ has some $a_i$ divisible by $Mp^r$, in particular $a_i\ge M$.
Every cubic form at which some $SL_n$-invariant of positive degree does not vanish satisfies the span condition, in every coordinate basis.

Suppose the support of $F$ consists of cubes and monomials $x_i^2x_j$ only, and $F$ satisfies the span condition. If a diagonal matrix $A$ of finite two-power order fixes $F$, then $\ord(\det A)\le2^{n-1}$. If equality holds, then after a permutation of the variables the support is exactly \begin{equation} x_1^2x_2,\ x_2^2x_3,\ \dots,\ x_{n-1}^2x_n,\ x_n^3, \end{equation} the eigenvalues of $A$ are $\xi,\xi^{-2},\xi^4,\dots,\xi^{(-2)^{n-1}}=1$ with $\xi$ of order $2^{n-1}$, and a diagonal substitution turns $F$ into the chain cubic $F_n=x_1^2x_2+\dots+x_{n-1}^2x_n+x_n^3$.

Let $F$ be a cubic form in $n\ge2$ variables satisfying the span condition, and let a diagonal matrix $A$ of finite two-power order fix $F$. Then $\ord(\det A)\le2^{n-1}$. If equality holds, then after a permutation of the variables the support of $F$ is exactly \eqref{eq:chainsupport}, $A$ has order $2^{n-1}$, and a diagonal substitution turns $F$ into $F_n$. The bound is attained by $F_n$.

For every $n\ge2$ and $s\ge0$, \[ \tr\bigl(\tau\mid(R_n)_s\bigr)=b_n(s),\qquad k_n(s)\equiv b_n(s)\pmod3 , \] and $k_n(s)-b_n(s)$ is a nonnegative multiple of three. Hence $K_n(t)\equiv B_n(t)\pmod{3\Z[[t]]}$.
For every $n\ge2$, the stabilizer of $z_n$ in $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ is zero, so the stabilizer of $z_n$ in $GL_n$ is finite.

Let $n\ge2$, $M=2^{n-1}$, $\zeta$ a primitive $M$-th root of unity, and $X_n=\Spec T_n$. \begin{enumerate} \item The $SL_n$-orbit of $z_n$ is closed; its stabilizer in $GL_n$ is cyclic of order $M$, generated by \begin{equation} g=\diag(\zeta^{w_1},\dots,\zeta^{w_n}),\qquad w_i=(-2)^{i-1}\bmod M , \end{equation} on which $\det$ is faithful; its stabilizer in $SL_n$ is trivial. \item The nonzero closed points of $X_n$ fixed by the grading group $\mu_M$ form one orbit of the grading group $\Gm$, the orbit of the image $p_n$ of $z_n$, whose stabilizer in $\Gm$ is exactly $\mu_M$. $X_n$ is smooth at $p_n$, and the fixed scheme $X_n^{\zeta}$ is smooth of dimension one there. \item $B_n$ has a simple pole at every primitive $M$-th root of unity $\xi$, with $\lim_{t\to\xi}(1-t^M)B_n(t)$ a unit in $\Z[\xi,1/2]$. \item If the two-part of an integer $d$ is at least $M$ and $d\ne M$, then $B_n$ is regular at every primitive $d$-th root of unity; in particular at the primitive $M3^r$-th roots for $r\ge1$. \end{enumerate}

For every $n\ge2$ there is $r\ge0$ such that $K_n(t)=\sum_sg((s^n),(s^n), (s^n))t^s$ has a pole at every primitive root of unity of order $2^{n-1}3^r$. Every expression $K_n(t)=P(t)/\prod_i(1-t^{a_i})^{b_i}$ with $P\in\Q[t]$ and positive integers $a_i,b_i$ has some $a_i$ divisible by $2^{n-1}3^r$; in particular every positive form of $K_n$ has modular index at least $2^{n-1}$.

The existence clause of PH3 for Kronecker coefficients \cite[Hypothesis 3.3.4]{GCT6} fails: for the inputs $((1^n),(1^n),(1^n))$, with $\rank(x)=n^2+5n$, every positive rational form of the generating function has modular index at least $2^{n-1}$. The relaxed PH3 of \cite[Appendix, p.~20]{BOR}, which bounds the modular index of the minimal positive form by a polynomial in the largest height $h=n$, fails as well.

Let $F_n=x_1^2x_2+x_2^2x_3+\dots+x_{n-1}^2x_n+x_n^3$ and $p_n\in X$ its image. \begin{enumerate} \item $F_n$ defines a smooth hypersurface, and its $SL_n$-orbit is closed. \item Every linear transformation preserving $F_n$ up to a scalar is a scalar multiple of a diagonal matrix $\diag(a_1,a_1^{-2},a_1^4,\dots,a_1^{(-2)^{n-1}})$ with $a_1^{3M}=1$. These matrices form the stabilizer of $F_n$ in $GL_n$, a cyclic group of order $3M$; the stabilizer in $SL_n$ is the scalar group $\mu_\nu$, which acts trivially on cubic forms. \item The stabilizer of $p_n$ in the grading group is exactly $\mu_M$. \item $X$ is smooth at $p_n$, and for a primitive $M$-th root of unity $\zeta$ the fixed scheme $X^\zeta$ is smooth of dimension one at $p_n$. \end{enumerate}

Let $n\ge4$ and $M=2^{n-1}$. \begin{enumerate} \item The support of the fixed scheme $X^{\mu_M}$ is the closure $Y$ of the grading orbit of $p_n$, and $X$ is smooth along $Y\setminus\{0\}$. \item $H_n$ has a simple pole at every primitive $M$-th root of unity $\zeta$, with \begin{equation} \mathcal C_n(\zeta):=\lim_{t\to\zeta}(1-t^M)H_n(t) =\frac1{\det\bigl(1-\zeta\mid N^*_{Y/X,\eta_Y}\bigr)}\ne0 . \end{equation} \item If $\eta$ is a root of unity whose order $q$ has two-part at least $M$, then $H_n$ has a pole at $\eta$ if and only if $q=M$. \item In every expression $H_n(t)=P(t)/\prod_j(1-t^{a_j})^{b_j}$ with $P\in\C[t]$ and $a_j,b_j>0$, some $a_j$ is divisible by $M$. \end{enumerate}

For $n\ge4$, every positive rational form of $H_n$ has modular index at least $2^{n-1}$, while $\dim GL_m+\operatorname{ht}(\lambda)+\operatorname{ht}(\pi) =m^2+n+1=O(n^6)$ and $\rank(x)=2n+m+1$. The existence clause of \cite[Hypothesis 1.6.7]{GCT6}, and so also its specific clause on the minimal positive form, fails for plethysm coefficients; so does \cite[Hypothesis 3.3.4]{GCT6} for the plethysm problem.

Let $L$ be the least common multiple of the orders of the poles of $H_n$, a period of $f_n$, and write $f_n(s)=q_r(s)$ for $s\equiv r\pmod L$. Then $v_2(L)=n-1$, and for every residue $r$ and every $X$, \begin{equation} q_r(X)-q_{r+L/2}(X)=2W_n(r). \end{equation} Consequently $f_n(x)\ge2W_n(x)$ for every integer $x\ge p(f_n)$ and every integer $x\ge s(f_n)+1$. In particular, if $2W_n(x)>f_n(x)$ for an integer $x\ge0$, then $p(f_n)>x$ and $s(f_n)\ge x$.
For every odd $a$, \begin{equation} \mathcal C_n(\zeta^a)=\prod_{b\in\mathcal S_n}\bigl(1-\zeta^{a\nu b}\bigr)^{-1}. \end{equation}

For every $n\ge4$, \begin{equation} \log_2|Z_n|\ge\binom n4-3\binom{n-1}3-(n-1)(n-2)-\binom n3-(n-1) \ge\frac{n^4}{24}-2n^3 . \end{equation} If $n\ge6$ and $E_n\le|Z_n|/4$, then for every integer $X$ there is an integer $x$ with $X\le x\le X+8$ and $W_n(x)\ge|Z_n|/4$.
If $E_n\le|Z_n|/4$ for all sufficiently large $n$, then for every real $0<c<1/4$ and all sufficiently large $n$, $p(f_n)>2^{cn}$ and $s(f_n)\ge2^{cn}$.

For $n\ge5$ and odd $a$, $P_n(a)=J_n(a)\,P_{n-1}(-a\bmod M_{n-1})$. The selected sibling ratio satisfies \begin{equation} \delta_n:=\frac{P_n(b_n+M_{n-1})}{P_n(b_n)}\le2^{-n^3/6+4n^2-107n/6+19}, \qquad\delta_n\le2^{-n^3/12}\ (n\ge48). \end{equation} If for some $0<\rho<1$ and all $n\ge n_0$ and all odd $a$ with $a\bmod M_{n-1}\notin\{\pm b_{n-1}\}$ \begin{equation} J_n(a)+J_n(a+M_{n-1})\le\rho J_n(b_n), \end{equation} then $Q_n\le\rho Q_{n-1}+2\delta_n$ for $n\ge n_0$, and $Q_n\to0$.

Let $1\le r\le3$, integers $1\le q_1<\dots<q_r$, signs $\epsilon_i$, $\kappa\in\Z$, $J\ge1$ odd, $R=\lceil\log_2(16J)\rceil$, and $x=\kappa/3+(J/3)\sum_i\epsilon_i2^{-q_i}$. Then $\|x\|_{\mathbb R/\Z}\ge 1/(6\cdot2^{q_1+(r-1)R})$. In particular, if $q_1\le R$, then $2^{-3R-1}\le|1-e^{2\pi ix}|\le2$.

near increments: For odd $1\le j<M$, with $a_j\equiv j\cdot3^{-1}\pmod M$ and $R=\lceil\log_2(16j)\rceil$, and $n\ge5$, \begin{equation} \Bigl|\log_2\frac{J_n(a_j)}{J_n(b_n)}+\binom{n-1}2\log_2j -\mathbf1_{3\mid j}\binom n2\Bigr|\le100nR^2 . \end{equation} For $\delta=10^{-5}$ and odd $3\le j\le2^{\delta n}$ this gives $\log_2(J_n(a_j)/J_n(b_n))\le-n^2\log_2j/12$.

far increments: Let $n\ge5$, $l=n-1$, $M=2^l$, $a$ odd, $j\equiv3a\pmod M$ with $1\le j<M$, and $J=\min\{j,M-j\}$. Then \begin{equation} \log_2\frac{J_n(a)}{J_n(b_n)}\le7n^2-\frac{(\log_2J-8)_+^3}{24}. \end{equation} In particular, for $\delta>0$, $J\ge2^{\delta n}$ and $n\ge\max\{5,16/\delta,2688/\delta^3\}$, the ratio is at most $2^{-\delta^3n^3/384}$.

$E_n/|Z_n|\to0$. Consequently, for every real $0<c<1/4$ and all sufficiently large $n$, \[ p(f_n)>2^{cn},\qquad s(f_n)\ge2^{cn}, \] and $p(f_n)>2^{n/8}$, $s(f_n)\ge2^{n/8}$ for every $n\ge2\cdot10^{80}$.

Hypotheses 1.6.5(a) (SH) and 1.6.6 (PH2) of \cite{GCT6} fail for the plethysm coefficients of the ray $\mu=(3)$, $\lambda=(d_0)$, $\pi=((3/\nu)^n)$: the indices exceed every polynomial in $h=m^2+n+1=\Theta(n^6)$. Hypotheses 3.3.2(a) and 3.3.3 fail for the plethysm problem with $\rank(x)=2n+m+1$.

For $N\ge2$ let $\rho_N:\Gm\to GL_2$, $\rho_N(t)=\diag(t^{N+1},t)$, let $\pi=(1)$ (the representation $\C^2$, stretched to $\Sym^n\C^2$) and $\lambda$ the character $t\mapsto t^2$ (stretched to $t^{2n}$). Then \[ f_N(n)=\dim\Hom_{\Gm}\bigl(t^{2n},\Sym^n(\C^2)|_{\rho_N}\bigr)=\mathbf1_{N\mid n}, \qquad \sum_{n\ge0}f_N(n)T^n=\frac1{1-T^N}, \] and every expression of this series as $P(T)/\prod_i(1-T^{a_i})^{b_i}$ has some $a_i$ divisible by $N$, while $\rank(x)=1+2+1+1=5$. Hypothesis 3.3.4 of \cite{GCT6} fails for subgroup restriction as stated.

For odd $N\ge3$ let $\sigma_N:\Gm\to GL_3$, $\sigma_N(t)=\diag(t,t^3,t^{N+1})$, with $\pi=(1)$ and $\lambda=t^2$ as before. Then \[ g_N(n)=\#\{(b,c)\in\Z_{\ge0}^2:2b+Nc=n\},\qquad \sum_{n\ge0}g_N(n)T^n=\frac1{(1-T^2)(1-T^N)}, \] and $p(g_N)=s(g_N)=N-2$, while $\rank(x)=1+3+1+1=6$. Hypotheses 3.3.2(a) and 3.3.3 of \cite{GCT6} fail for subgroup restriction as stated.
